title: Mechanistic Insights into TMPyP4 Recognition of the HIV-1 LTR-III G-Quadruplex in Dilute and Protein Condensate Environments Reveal Hidden Dual Binding Modes
authors: Susmita Pradhan; Shailesh Mani Tripathi; Shubhangi Sharma; Arun Pratap Singh; Sandeep Sundriyal; Satyajit Patra
one_liner_zh: 该文通过荧光光谱、分子对接和MD模拟研究TMPyP4与HIV-1 LTR-III G-四链体的双模式结合，虽涉及蛋白-DNA互作和物理模拟方法，但对象为配体-GQ而非TF-DNA体系，且未聚焦转录因子结合机制，故属广义蛋白-DNA互作的可借鉴文献。
abstract: G-quadruplex (GQ) structures within the HIV-1 long terminal repeat (LTR) regulate viral transcription and represent promising antiviral targets; however, detailed mechanistic understanding of their ligand recognition at the molecular level remains limited and has largely been investigated under dilute conditions despite the crowded and compartmentalized nature of intracellular environment. Here, we investigate the interaction of the cationic porphyrin TMPyP4 with the HIV-1 LTR-III GQ under dilute conditions and inside protein-rich phase-separated condensates that mimic intracellular biocondensates. Steady-state and time-resolved fluorescence measurements reveal a dual binding behavior that is not discernible from absorption spectroscopy. A high-affinity guanine-rich binding mode leads to efficient fluorescence quenching through electron transfer from ground-state guanine to excited TMPyP4, whereas a weaker non-guanine binding mode gives rise to enhanced and long-lived emission. Nucleotide-specific control experiments validate the origin of these distinct binding environments. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations further support preferential binding of TMPyP4 at the terminal G-quartet together with a secondary binding mode near the quadruplex–duplex junction. Importantly, both TMPyP4 and LTR-III GQ preferentially partition into the condensates, where the hybrid GQ structure, dual binding behavior, and associated excited-state signatures remain preserved despite the crowded and viscous environment. Although a slight reduction in binding affinity is observed inside the condensates, the overall binding mechanism remains largely preserved due to compensatory effects arising from the condensate microenvironment. Overall, this work demonstrates that ligand recognition of viral GQ remains preserved within protein condensates and establishes fluorescence spectroscopy as a sensitive approach for resolving hidden binding heterogeneity in GQ–ligand interactions.
abstract_zh: G-四链体（G-quadruplex, GQ）结构位于HIV-1长末端重复序列（long terminal repeat, LTR）中，调控病毒转录并代表有前景的抗病毒靶点；然而，对其配体识别在分子水平上的详细机制理解仍然有限，且大多在稀释条件下研究，尽管细胞内环境具有拥挤和区室化的特性。在此，我们研究了阳离子卟啉TMPyP4与HIV-1 LTR-III GQ在稀释条件下以及模拟细胞内生物凝聚体的富含蛋白质的相分离凝聚体中的相互作用。稳态和时间分辨荧光测量揭示了一种从吸收光谱中无法辨别的双重结合行为。高亲和力的富含鸟嘌呤结合模式通过从基态鸟嘌呤到激发态TMPyP4的电子转移导致高效荧光猝灭，而较弱的非鸟嘌呤结合模式则产生增强且长寿命的发射。核苷酸特异性对照实验验证了这些不同结合环境的来源。分子对接和分子动力学模拟进一步支持TMPyP4优先结合于末端G-四联体，同时在四链体-双链体连接处附近存在次级结合模式。重要的是，TMPyP4和LTR-III GQ均优先分配进入凝聚体，其中尽管环境拥挤且粘稠，杂交GQ结构、双重结合行为及相关激发态特征仍得以保留。尽管在凝聚体内观察到结合亲和力略有降低，但由于凝聚体微环境产生的补偿效应，整体结合机制在很大程度上得以保持。总体而言，这项工作证明了病毒GQ的配体识别在蛋白质凝聚体内得以保留，并确立了荧光光谱法作为解析GQ-配体相互作用中隐藏结合异质性的灵敏方法。
